title: Odorizzi v. Bloomfield School District
lead: A teacher alleged that officials obtained his immediate resignation while he was exhausted after arrest; the complaint sufficiently alleged undue influence even though its other rescission theories failed.

actors.name: Donald Odorizzi
actors.role: Elementary teacher seeking to rescind his resignation

actors.name: Superintendent and principal
actors.role: Officials alleged to have pressed for immediate resignation

proceedings: Trial court: sustained demurrer to amended complaint without leave and dismissed.
California Court of Appeal: reversed because undue influence was adequately pleaded.
limits: The court did not find pressure proved, rescind the resignation, order reinstatement, or decide continued fitness to teach or rescission timeliness. The criminal-law and employment-law setting is historical.

review.basis: Individually written and compared with the canonical full brief; no new independent opinion audit claimed.

sections.title: Arrest and resignation occur within two days
sections.cue: Introduce the employment and what happened afterward.
paragraphs: Donald Odorizzi taught elementary school for Bloomfield School District in 1964 and held a permanent-employee contract for the following year. On June 10, he was arrested on charges the historical opinion described as homosexual activity. He signed and delivered a resignation June 11, and the district accepted June 13. The charges were dismissed in July under Penal Code § 995, not resolved by a reported trial acquittal. In September he sought to return; the district refused, and he sued.

His amended complaint said arrest, questioning, booking, bail, and forty hours without sleep left severe emotional strain and inability to think clearly. While he was in that state, the superintendent and principal came to his apartment. They allegedly professed concern for him, demanded immediate resignation, and said there was no time for counsel. Refusal would mean suspension, dismissal, and humiliating publicity; immediate resignation supposedly would avoid publicity and preserve other teaching prospects. He alleged confidence in their assurances and pressure displaced his judgment.

sections.title: The court rejects several rescission theories without rejecting every account of pressure
sections.cue: Explain the statutory grounds and failed allegations.
paragraphs: The trial court sustained a demurrer without leave to amend and dismissed. On appeal, Justice Fleming examined whether facts, not merely a label of involuntary action, supported rescission under Civil Code §§ 1689 and 1567.

Duress and menace required unlawful acts or threats. Unwelcome legal proceedings were not unlawful merely because threatened; knowingly false claims presented a different situation. As pleaded, the officials described suspension and dismissal measures that the then-applicable Education Code authorized and required. Publicity incidental to good-faith performance did not establish unlawfulness. That conclusion did not declare all publicity threats lawful or make timing and manner irrelevant to other grounds.

Actual fraud lacked adequate allegations of knowledge, inducing intent, and justified reliance. Constructive fraud required a duty from a confidential or fiduciary relationship; ordinary employment alone did not establish one, especially in termination negotiations where each side protected its interests. Mistake also failed because participants knew the material circumstances and principally predicted consequences. Later dismissal of charges did not prove an existing factual or legal mistake about the transaction.

sections.title: Mental weakness and excessive persuasion can combine into undue influence
sections.cue: State the doctrine without requiring complete incapacity.
paragraphs: Civil Code § 1575 covered unfair exploitation of mental weakness or grossly oppressive use of necessities and distress. Misrepresentation and a confidential or authoritative relationship were not indispensable under that branch. Failure to plead fraud therefore did not defeat undue influence.

The court considered susceptibility and pressure together. Susceptibility could fall below total incapacity under § 38 or lesser incapacity under § 39. Age, health, emotional anguish, and temporary exhaustion could compromise free choice without permanent disability. Arrest-related strain and forty sleepless hours sufficiently put vulnerability in issue, without proving actual incapacity.

Pressure could be ordinary force applied to weakened capacity or extraordinary force applied to ordinary capacity. The question was displacement of independent judgment. Regret, bad bargains, normal sales persuasion, and disappointed expectations of appreciating land were insufficient by themselves.

sections.title: Several pleaded features match a recognizable pattern of overpersuasion
sections.cue: Apply the indicators while keeping other cases and hypotheticals separate.
paragraphs: The court listed recurring indicators: inappropriate timing, unusual place, urgency, dire consequences of delay, several persuaders against one, absence of independent advisers, and claims that time prevented consultation. These were interacting signs, not seven mandatory elements or a numerical automatic rule.

Its examples came from other cases: Moore involved relatives pressing a pregnant widow after violent bereavement and a funeral; Weger concerned a hospital patient in a cast, pain, and nervous distress; Fyan involved an unannounced 1 a.m. demand for a commission agreement before morning despite requests for time. They illustrated rather than supplemented Odorizzi’s history.

A measured business-hours discussion after an interval, explanation of lawful options, access to advice, and overnight reflection would present a weaker pressure claim. That was a hypothetical contrast. The actual pleading instead described two officials at an exhausted man’s apartment, insisting on immediate action, discouraging counsel, stressing exposure, and promising help. Together, alleged subjective weakness and objective pressure warranted factual examination.

sections.title: Reversal permits proof of undue influence rather than deciding it
paragraphs: Whether officials merely influenced a free judgment or dominated it could not be resolved from the pleading alone. On November 3, 1966, the Court of Appeal reversed dismissal because the amended complaint stated a rescission claim for undue influence. Presiding Justice Roth and Justice Herndon joined Fleming without separate opinions.

The court did not itself undo the resignation, reinstate Odorizzi, find misconduct proved, decide whether he should continue teaching, or resolve timely rescission under § 1691. It allowed the sufficient theory to proceed while rejecting the other pleaded grounds on their existing allegations.
